**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| Capability | What Turbonomic Does | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|------------|----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | Collects real‑time telemetry (CPU, memory, I/O, network, latency) from on‑prem, GCP, AWS, Azure, and other private clouds into a single data plane. | Unilever can see the health of its entire digital estate—whether it’s running on Google Kubernetes Engine, Amazon EKS, or Azure AKS—without having to open multiple dashboards. |
| **Predictive Capacity Planning** | Uses machine learning models trained on historical usage patterns to forecast future demand spikes, storage growth, and compute needs. | Enables proactive scaling before performance degrades, saving Unilever from costly over‑provisioning or unexpected outages during peak seasons (e.g., holiday sales). |
| **Automated Remediation & Optimization** | Continuously applies business rules (SLAs, cost budgets, compliance constraints) to recommend or automatically move workloads to the most efficient resource pool. | Reduces manual toil for Unilever’s ops teams; ensures workloads run where they’re cheapest and meet performance targets without human intervention. |
| **Cost Transparency & Forecasting** | Aggregates spend per workload, service, or business unit and projects future bills based on current utilization trends. | Gives Unilever finance and product managers clear visibility into which campaigns or product lines consume the most cloud resources, supporting better budgeting decisions. |
| **Policy‑Based Governance** | Lets Unilever define policies such as “no more than X% of workloads on spot instances” or “must stay within Y% of budget.” | Ensures compliance with corporate governance and regulatory requirements while still allowing flexibility for innovation. |
| **Integration with CI/CD Pipelines** | Exposes APIs that can trigger capacity adjustments or cost alerts directly from build/deploy pipelines. | Allows Unilever’s DevOps teams to incorporate capacity planning into automated release workflows, reducing surprises at deployment time. |

---

### Difference Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Provider Tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | Native GCP/AWS/Azure Tool |
|---------|------------|---------------------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud (multi‑tenant, multi‑region, hybrid) | Single‑provider focus |
| **Data Model** | Unified abstraction layer that normalizes metrics across providers | Provider‑specific metric schemas |
| **Decision Engine** | AI/ML‑driven recommendation engine that learns from your own workloads | Rule‑based or simple threshold alerts |
| **Automation** | Can push changes back to provider APIs (auto‑scale, migrate, reallocate) | Typically requires manual action or separate automation scripts |
| **Governance Layer** | Policy engine that enforces SLAs, budgets, and compliance rules | Basic tagging or IAM roles; no built‑in policy enforcement |
| **Cost Modeling** | Predictive forecasting using historical data + provider pricing APIs | Static cost calculators or billing reports |
| **Observability Depth** | Adds context (business impact, risk scores, dependency graphs) | Raw metrics and logs only |
| **Vendor Lock‑In Risk** | Vendor‑agnostic platform; you control the data | Tied to a specific cloud ecosystem |

**Bottom Line:**  
Turbonomic acts as a *single pane of glass* that not only visualizes but also *acts upon* the data from all of Unilever’s cloud environments. While each cloud provider offers powerful monitoring and cost tools, those tools work in silos and lack the cross‑domain intelligence and automation that Turbonomic brings. For a global consumer goods company like Unilever, this unified, AI‑powered approach means faster decision making, tighter cost controls, and higher confidence that IT services will meet both performance and regulatory expectations.
